title: Replacing Dev Workflow Scripts with Claude Code Skills and Plugins
summary: Nate Little replaces a set of Python feature scripts with Claude Code skills packaged as a plugin.
learn: Little describes the previous workflow: Python scripts for feature start, rebase and merge, plus a create PRD command that pulls a Linear ticket and interviews the developer.
A skill combines prompts with bash or Python code, so deterministic steps run as code while the agent handles edge cases such as a branch name that already exists.
Little says a skill loads only its front matter description into context, reads SKILL.md when invoked, and loads other files in its folder as needed, which helps when MCPs inflate context.
Little keeps slash commands as one-line wrappers that call skills, and uses a sub-agent only for a log reviewer, because sub-agents get their own context and return a short summary.
Live demo: a feature start command takes a Linear ticket number, runs a PRD interview with multiple choice questions, then offers a work tree and Taskmaster task generation.
The workflow is packaged as a plugin in a marketplace: one marketplace JSON file, one JSON file per plugin, and folders for commands, agents, scripts and skills.
